CausalChain: Icaritin inhibits IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 signaling -> Reduced PD-L1 expression on HCC cells -> Decreased T cell exhaustion and improved CD8+ T cell activity; Additionally, Icaritin modulates ERα36 signaling -> Dampening proliferative and immune evasion signals in HBV-related HCC -> Synergizes with PD-1/PD-L1 blockade -> Enhanced anti-tumor immune response.
Hypothesis: In HCC, particularly in HBV-associated tumors with high ERα36 and PD-L1 expression, Icaritin treatment will reprogram the tumor microenvironment by reducing PD-L1 levels and modulating ERα36-mediated oncogenic signals, thereby enhancing the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits a highly complex tumor microenvironment characterized by both oncogenic signaling and immunosuppressive features. Emerging data indicate that traditional Chinese medicine compounds such as Icaritin, which acts via modulation of ERα36 and downregulation of the IL-6/JAK2/STAT3/PD-L1 axis, may not only directly inhibit tumor proliferation but also re‐shape the immune landscape. Here, we hypothesize that Icaritin can sensitize HCC to immune checkpoint blockade by reducing PD-L1 expression and modulating ERα36 driven oncogenic signals, ultimately enhancing CD8+ T cell mediated responses in a subset of HBV‐related HCC. Biomarker stratification based on ERα36 and PD-L1 levels may help to identify patients who are most likely to benefit from such combination treatments.
